Hanzo Digital Credential Infrastructure

Work-authorization credentials held on the person's own device. Issued over OpenID4VCI, presented over OpenID4VP, encoded as ISO mdoc, anchored in X.509 PKI.

  • Local issuer
  • Issuance and lifecycle orchestration
  • Holder demo
  • Verifier with a trust registry

660synthetic tests, plus senior and security review

A synthetic MVP and pilot foundation. It makes no production or government claims.

TypeScript, on the identity side

Illustrative · mock signature result

Credential precheck

What it proves

The four gates a verifier passes before trusting anything: signature, trusted issuer, an expiry that actually parses, then the clock. The clock is injectable, so the check is testable.

What it does not do

No cryptography. The mock flag stands in for the real check. The issuer sits on .invalid, a domain reserved so it never resolves.

Read the file on GitHub
Illustrative · every check is a stand-in

Verifier gates

Rewritten from scratch for this page. Inspired by the verifier service in the credential work, which enforces its checks in a fixed order.

  1. Gate 1

    Purpose

    "purpose not allowed"

  2. Gate 2

    Nonce

    "nonce already used"

  3. Gate 3

    Issuer

    "issuer not trusted"

  4. Gate 4

    Revocation

    "credential revoked"

  5. Gate 5

    Disclosure

    "requested field not disclosable"

What it proves

Fail-fast ordered verification, purpose binding, replay protection via a single-use nonce, revocation handling, and minimal disclosure.

What it does not do

No cryptography, no real issuer, no real credential format. Every check is a stand-in.

Illustrative · not the real lifecycle engine

Lifecycle transitions

Rewritten from scratch for this page. Inspired by the issuance and lifecycle orchestration in the credential work.

Allowed transitions, from row to column
from \ toissuedsuspendedrevokedexpired
issuednoyesyesyes
suspendedyesnoyesyes

What it proves

Domain modeling with fail-closed terminal states. Revoked and expired have no exits.

What it does not do

Not the real lifecycle engine, no persistence, no real events.
